evidence_class: MEASURED (Vitis HLS 2020.2 csim + csynth on this machine)

provenance.datatypes_csim_csynth: ap_int<10> act, ap_int<32> acc, ap_int<20> lut (ap_types.h under -DHLS_USE_AP_INT)
provenance.note_on_target: xc7z020clg400-1 is the PROVISIONAL measurement part; final board not selected (AGENTS.md).

changes_vs_baseline: context accumulation restructured j-outer / HD-unrolled (bit-exact reorder)

#pragma HLS INLINE on attention0_row, attention0_kv, and linear (required so the v partition reaches the context loop AND to keep each linear call site's Din compile-time-constant; without the linear inline the shared linear has a variable-Din inner loop and transformer_core latency becomes unbounded '?')
optimized_v1_aggressive_inline_MEASURED.csim_ap_int: 16/16 exact golden vectors, 0 errors (Vitis, ap_int widths)

measured_comparison_v1_vs_baseline.bram_overflow_root_cause: weight-ROM replication from inlining linear (its inner MAC loop unrolls, forcing multi-port weight ROMs). finish_token FFN alone: W_l0_ff3=126 BRAM, W_l0_ff0=62 BRAM. The v cyclic partition itself is cheap (v_V_0..7 = 24 BRAM total).

optimized_v2_noinline_HANG.changes_vs_baseline: context reorder + cyclic v partition ONLY (no explicit INLINE)
optimized_v2_noinline_HANG.interpretation: 2020.2 scheduler stalls when the cyclic-partitioned v is passed by pointer to a non-inlined attention0_row; consistent with the known 2020.2 code-transformation stall on this design at SEQ=1024

realtime_assessment.conclusion: MEASURED 2.0x latency improvement, but (a) v1 overflows Z7020 BRAM so it does not fit as-is, and (b) even at 2.0x the core is still ~18x slower than the continuous non-overlapping 50 kHz input rate. Real-time is NOT achieved and NOT claimed.

verification_summary.gpp_native_width_ab_vs_baseline: byte-identical (distinct from the ap_int check above)

recommended_next_optimization: Retain the context parallelism but stop the weight-ROM replication that overflows BRAM: cap linear's inner-loop unrolling / bind multiplier+ROM instances (e.g. HLS ALLOCATION, or pipeline the inner MAC loop so weights stay single-port), OR copy each head's V-slice into a small locally-partitioned buffer inside a still-separate attention function (avoids the pointer-partition scheduler hang). Then re-measure fit on xc7z020clg400-1.

changes_vs_v1: generic runtime-dim `linear` replaced by compile-time template linear_fixed<ROWS,DIN,DOUT> (constant loop bounds; NOT force-inlined; one shared module per shape)
inner MAC (Din) reduction loop pipelined instead of outer loop -> single weight read per cycle -> weight ROMs single-port, NOT replicated
v projection written by an in-scope loop inside inlined attention0_kv (partitioned v never crosses a non-inlined function pointer -> avoids the v2 code-transformation hang)
context j-outer/HD=8-unrolled loop and cyclic v partition kept identical to v1 (the speedup; bit-exact)
optimized_v3_bram_fixed_MEASURED.weight_rom_replication_removed: CONFIRMED from hierarchy: W_l0_wq/out/cls1 now 1 BRAM each (were 31); finish_token (ff0/ff3) 14 BRAM (was 198)
optimized_v3_bram_fixed_MEASURED.note_vs_v1: 1.65x vs v1's 2.007x; v3 trades ~18% latency for fitting the device (v1 overflowed BRAM at 136%). Fitting has priority over max speed.

headline_conclusion: v3 is the recommended candidate: MEASURED 1.65x faster than baseline AND fits xc7z020clg400-1 (all four resources within capacity). Real-time (48.83 wps) still NOT achieved (gap ~22x) and board-readiness still requires implementation/bitstream + hardware validation.
